You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# QuickJS

QuickJS is a small and embeddable JavaScript engine. It supports the ES2023 specification including modules, asynchronous generators, proxies, and BigInt.

## Features

- Small and easily embeddable: a few C files, no external dependency
- Fast interpreter with very low startup time
- Almost complete ES2023 support (including modules, async generators, proxies, BigInt)
- Passes nearly 100% of the ECMAScript Test Suite (test262)
- Can compile JavaScript to executables with no external dependency
- Garbage collection using reference counting with cycle removal
- Mathematical extensions: BigDecimal, BigFloat, operator overloading
- Built-in `std` and `os` modules for system interaction

## Usage

### Run a JavaScript file
```
qjs [options] file.js [args...]
```

### Evaluate an expression
```
qjs -e "console.log('hello')"
```

### Interactive REPL
```
qjs -i
```

### Options
```
-h  --help              list options
-e  --eval EXPR         evaluate EXPR
-i  --interactive       go to interactive mode
-m  --module            load as ES6 module (default=autodetect)
    --script            load as ES6 script (default=autodetect)
    --strict            force strict mode
-I  --include file      include an additional file
    --std               make 'std' and 'os' available to the loaded script
-T  --trace             trace memory allocation
-d  --dump              dump memory usage stats
    --memory-limit n    limit memory usage to n bytes
    --stack-size n      limit stack size to n bytes
-s                      strip all debug info
    --strip-source      strip the source code
-q  --quit              just instantiate the interpreter and quit
```

### std module
Provides: `printf`, `sprintf`, `open`, `popen`, `tmpfile`, `puts`, `getline`,
`readFile`, `loadFile`, `strerror`, `exit`, `gc`, `getenv`, `setenv`,
`unsetenv`, `getenviron`, `urlGet`, `parseExtJSON`, `SEEK_SET`, `SEEK_CUR`,
`SEEK_END`, `Error`.

### os module
Provides: `open`, `close`, `seek`, `read`, `write`, `isatty`, `ttyGetWinSize`,
`ttySetRaw`, `remove`, `rename`, `realpath`, `getcwd`, `chdir`, `mkdir`,
`stat`, `lstat`, `utimes`, `symlink`, `readlink`, `readdir`, `setReadHandler`,
`setWriteHandler`, `signal`, `exec`, `waitpid`, `pipe`, `kill`, `sleep`,
`setTimeout`, `clearTimeout`, `platform`, `Worker`.

"""Development-only black-box comparison of our test inputs.

The reference is supplied as an explicit command-line argument. It is never
used by the implementation or by the build.
"""
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
cases=json.loads((Path(__file__).parent/'behavior_cases.json').read_text())
reference=sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv)>1 else './executable'
ours=sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv)>2 else './.build/executable'
failed=[]
for name,code,flags in cases:
    if len(sys.argv)>3 and name not in sys.argv[3:]:continue
    results=[]
    for exe in (reference,ours):
        try:
            p=subprocess.run([exe]+flags+['-e',code],capture_output=True,timeout=10)
            results.append((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr))
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:results.append(('timeout',e.stdout,e.stderr))
    if results[0]!=results[1]:
        failed.append(name)
        print('\nFAIL',name,'\nCODE:',code,'\nREF:',results[0],'\nNEW:',results[1],flush=True)
    else:print('OK',name,flush=True)
print('\nFailures:',len(failed),failed)

"""Development-only black-box comparison of our test inputs.

The reference is supplied as an explicit command-line argument. It is never
used by the implementation or by the build.
"""
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
cases=json.loads((Path(__file__).parent/'behavior_cases.json').read_text())
reference=sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv)>1 else './executable'
ours=sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv)>2 else './.build/executable'
failed=[]
for name,code,flags in cases:
    if len(sys.argv)>3 and name not in sys.argv[3:]:continue
    results=[]
    for exe in (reference,ours):
        try:
            p=subprocess.run([exe]+flags+['-e',code],capture_output=True,timeout=10)
            results.append((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr))
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:results.append(('timeout',e.stdout,e.stderr))
    if results[0]!=results[1]:
        failed.append(name)
        print('\nFAIL',name,'\nCODE:',code,'\nREF:',results[0],'\nNEW:',results[1],flush=True)
    else:print('OK',name,flush=True)
print('\nFailures:',len(failed),failed)

# Independent interpreter implementation

## Build

Run `./compile.sh` from the checkout. It checks the Python source and creates
an executable entry point named `executable` in the repository root. Python 3
and its standard library are the only requirements; the build does not fetch
packages or use an external JavaScript engine.

For development, `OUTPUT=.build/executable ./compile.sh` keeps the generated
entry point in a separate, ignored directory.

## Organization

* `syntax.py` implements tokenization and recursive-descent parsing, retaining
  locations and function source text.
* `validation.py` checks early errors before program execution.
* `values.py` supplies the value model, descriptors, indexed storage,
  conversions, and console formatting.
* `runtime.py` implements lexical environments, expression and statement
  evaluation, function calls, module binding, and event queues.
* `coroutines.py` represents suspended async and generator execution.
* `builtins.py` implements the standard objects and their methods.
* `host.py` and `workers.py` implement file, environment, operating-system,
  timer, and worker-message operations.
* `api.py` and `api_layout.json` describe the observed public property layout.
* `numeric.py` specializes a restricted side-effect-free numeric expression
  language; other code uses the general evaluator.
* `cli.py` handles options, diagnostics, file execution, and the REPL.

All engine and host behavior here is implemented by this codebase. Generated
entry points, bytecode caches, and local observation/build directories are
ignored by Git.

## Tests

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` runs self-contained regression tests.
The tests use `JS_EXECUTABLE` if set, otherwise the generated root executable.

`tests/compare.py REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION` is an optional development utility
for black-box differential testing of the inputs in `behavior_cases.json`.
It is not imported by the implementation and is not part of the build or
runtime.

"""Self-contained regression tests; no reference executable is needed."""
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
EXE=Path(os.environ.get('JS_EXECUTABLE',str(ROOT/'executable'))).resolve()

class InterpreterTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def run_js(self,code,*flags,stdin=None):
        return subprocess.run([str(EXE),*flags,'-e',code],input=stdin,capture_output=True,text=True,cwd=ROOT,timeout=10)
    def expect(self,code,output,*flags):
        p=self.run_js(code,*flags)
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0,p.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,'')
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout,output)
    def test_basic_language(self):
        self.expect('const square=x=>x*x;print([1,2,3].map(square));let sum=0;for(let i=0;i<5;i++)sum+=i;print(sum)', '[ 1, 4, 9 ]\n10\n')
    def test_closures_and_destructuring(self):
        self.expect('function make(x){return y=>x+y}const {a,...rest}={a:2,b:3};print(make(a)(4),rest);let fs=[];for(let i=0;i<3;i++)fs.push(()=>i);print(fs.map(f=>f()));','6 { b: 3 }\n[ 0, 1, 2 ]\n')
    def test_recursive_numbers(self):
        self.expect('function fib(n){return n<2?n:fib(n-1)+fib(n-2)}print(fib(25));','75025\n')
    def test_bigints_and_typed_arrays(self):
        self.expect('print((2n**64n).toString());let a=new Uint8Array([1,255,256]);print(a);print(BigInt.asIntN(8,255n))','18446744073709551616\nUint8Array(3) [ 1, 255, 0 ]\n-1n\n')
    def test_descriptors_and_collections(self):
        self.expect('let x={};Object.defineProperty(x,"a",{value:2,enumerable:true});print(x);print(new Map([["a",1]]),new Set([1,1,2]));','{ a: 2 }\nMap(1) { "a" => 1 } Set(2) { 1, 2 }\n')
    def test_json_and_unicode(self):
        self.expect(r"print(JSON.stringify('\ud800'));print('\ud83d\ude00'==='😀');print(JSON.stringify({a:JSON.rawJSON('12345678901234567890')}))",'"\\ud800"\ntrue\n{"a":12345678901234567890}\n')
    def test_regex_and_templates(self):
        self.expect(r"print('abc123'.replace(/(\d+)/,'[$1]'));print(String.raw`a\nb${2}`);print('😀a'.match(/./gu));",'abc[123]\na\\nb2\n[ "😀", "a" ]\n')
    def test_async_order(self):
        self.expect("async function f(){print('start');await 0;print('end');return 4}f().then(print);print('sync')",'start\nsync\nend\n4\n')
    def test_generators(self):
        self.expect('function* g(){let x=yield 1;yield x*2;return 3}let it=g();print(it.next());print(it.next(5));print(it.next());','{ value: 1, done: false }\n{ value: 10, done: false }\n{ value: 3, done: true }\n')
    def test_file_api(self):
        self.expect("let f=std.tmpfile();f.puts('a\\nb\\n');print(f.tell(),f.tello());f.seek(0,0);print(f.getline(),f.getline(),f.getline());print(f.close());",'4 4n\na b null\n0\n','--std')
    def test_timers(self):
        self.expect("os.setTimeout(()=>print('timer'),0);Promise.resolve().then(()=>print('promise'));print('sync')",'sync\npromise\ntimer\n','--std')
    def test_module_loading(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            root=Path(directory)
            (root/'dep.mjs').write_text('export let n=0;export function inc(){n++};export default x=>x*2;')
            (root/'main.mjs').write_text("import twice,{n,inc} from './dep.mjs';inc();print(n,twice(3));")
            p=subprocess.run([str(EXE),str(root/'main.mjs')],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=10)
            self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr),(0,'1 6\n',''))
    def test_script_arguments(self):
        p=subprocess.run([str(EXE),'-e','print(scriptArgs)','one','two'],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=10)
        self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr),(0,'[ "one", "two" ]\n',''))
    def test_diagnostics(self):
        p=self.run_js('foo()')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,1)
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,"ReferenceError: 'foo' is not defined\n    at <eval> (<cmdline>:1:1)\n")
        p=self.run_js('let a=;')
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,"SyntaxError: unexpected token in expression: ';'\n    at <cmdline>:1:7\n")
    def test_quit_and_help(self):
        p=subprocess.run([str(EXE),'-q','-e','print(1)'],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=10)
        self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr),(0,'',''))
        p=subprocess.run([str(EXE),'--help'],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=10)
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,1)
        self.assertTrue(p.stdout.startswith('QuickJS version 2025-09-13\nusage: qjs '))
    def test_repl_directives(self):
        p=subprocess.run([str(EXE),'-i'],input='\\h\n\\q\n',capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=10)
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0,p.stderr)
        self.assertIn('\\clear      clear the terminal\n',p.stdout)
        self.assertTrue(p.stdout.startswith('QuickJS - Type "\\h" for help\nqjs > '))

if __name__=='__main__':unittest.main()
